C0.quote: neural networks of various sizes can learn to profitably manipulate a given voting method
C0.note: Strategic manipulation of voting rules by a single voter; computational/learning approach.

C1.quote: we trained one or more “generations” of MLPs with that model size
C1.note: Experiments on synthetic utility profiles (uniform, spatial, Mallows) measuring manipulability; also SB as topic. Simulation is the method for most results.

C2.1.quote: a preference profile for (V, X) is a function P assigning

C2.2.quote: assigning to each i ∈ V a linear order Pi of X
C2.2.note: Linear orders; utilities used only as held attitudes.

C2.3.quote: A utility profile for (V, X) is a function U

C2.4.quote: a voter has an incentive to report an insincere preference
C2.4.note: Utility profile U separate from submitted order P'i; manipulation defined as submitting an order differing from sincere.

C3.1.quote: we focus on the case of a single manipulating voter
C3.1.note: Manipulator submits insincere rankings; other voters sincere (profiles induced from utilities).

C3.2.note: Other voters' sincerity is implied by P(U) induced from utilities, but no verbal statement found; limited info about 'how other voters will vote'.

C4.1.note: Input rank order induced by utilities.

C5.1.quote: we use the difference between the left and right-hand sides
C5.1.note: Profitability measured as expected utility gain of the manipulator, a voter utility criterion.

C5.2.quote: normalized by the greatest possible utility difference according to Ui
C5.2.note: Evaluated on held utilities separate from submitted ranking.

VOT.quote_behav: we focus on the case of a single manipulating voter
VOT.quote_info: we train neural networks to manipulate on the basis of different types of limited information
VOT.note: Manipulator strategic with limited info (and ideal manipulator with full info baseline); other voters' behaviour fixed by probability models (not stated as sincere in words).

C7.1.quote: we focus on the case of a single manipulating voter
C7.1.note: Manipulating voter STRAT vs other voters sampled from probability models (NONSTRAT), same type VOT; coded as differing behaviour within voters.

C7.2.quote: A single voter can almost never affect the outcome of a large election
C7.2.note: Reason for focusing on single manipulator; conclusion lists all-strategize as future work.

C8.1.note: Optimal manipulation by single voter given information; no equilibrium.
